name: TL072CDR
title: TL071, TL072, TL074 families: single, dual and quad JFET-input op amps, 4.5 V to 40 V
summary: General-purpose JFET-input op amps in single (TL071), dual (TL072) and quad (TL074) versions. The newer H die runs from 4.5 V to 40 V with 1 mV typical offset, 20 V/µs slew, 5.25 MHz bandwidth, about 940 µA per channel and an input range up to the positive rail; the original C, AC, BC, I and M grades run from ±15 V with picoamp bias currents and 20 V/µs slew. TL072CDR is the dual C grade in an 8-pin SOIC on a 2500-piece reel, rated 0 °C to 70 °C.

circuits.title: Inverting amplifier, gain -3.6
circuits.description: Amplifier 1 inverts and scales its input. The source drives the inverting input through RI, RF closes the loop from the output to the same node, and the non-inverting input is grounded, so the gain is -RF / RI. With 10 kΩ and 36 kΩ the gain is -3.6 and a ±0.5 V input swings the output about ±1.8 V. The supplies are ±12 V. Amplifier 2 is unused.

circuits.title: Non-inverting amplifier with supply bypass
circuits.description: Amplifier 1 as a non-inverting stage: the input reaches IN+ through RIN, RG returns IN- to ground and RF feeds the output back to IN-, so RF and RG set the gain. A low-ESR ceramic capacitor bypasses VCC+ to ground; a second one bypasses VCC- and is fitted only with a negative supply (on one supply VCC- is ground). Amplifier 2 is unused.

circuits.title: Unity-gain test circuit
circuits.description: Amplifier 1 as a voltage follower: the output is tied straight back to IN-, VI drives IN+, and the output is loaded by 100 pF and 2 kΩ in parallel to ground.

circuits.title: Gain-of-10 inverting test circuit

circuits.title: Input offset null, TL071C in the PS package
circuits.description: Only the single TL071C in the 8-pin SO (PS) package has offset null pins. A 100 kΩ potentiometer spans OFFSET N1 and OFFSET N2, and its wiper returns to VCC- through 1.5 kΩ; turning it trims the input offset voltage.

operation.text: TL071, TL072 and TL074 are single, dual and quad JFET-input op amps. The H-suffix parts (TL071H, TL072H, TL074H) use a newer die made on a modern process. Parts without H or M come from either the older or the newer flow, so either set of figures can apply; M parts use the older die. TL072CDR is the dual C grade in an 8-pin SOIC on a 2500-piece reel, rated 0 °C to 70 °C.

C grades are characterized from 0 °C to 70 °C, I grades from -40 °C to +85 °C, M grades from -55 °C to +125 °C and the H parts from -40 °C to +125 °C. The A and B grades of the C range have tighter offset limits (6 mV and 3 mV maximum at 25 °C against 10 mV).

The H die offers 1 mV typical offset, 20 V/µs slew, 940 µA per channel, an input common-mode range that includes the positive rail, built-in EMI and RF filtering, and operation across -40 °C to +125 °C.
THD is 0.003 % typical, low enough for audio paths, and the output slews at 20 V/µs.
There is no enable pin; the amplifiers run whenever supply is present, from a single supply or split supplies.
On the new die every input has diodes to both supplies. If an input can go more than 0.5 V beyond a rail, limit its current to 10 mA or less.
The output survives a continuous short to ground, one amplifier in the package at a time.
More than 36 V on a single supply, or split supplies beyond ±18 V, can damage the part permanently. The absolute maximum supply is 42 V for devices other than the NS and PS packages and the M grades.

Fit a 0.1 µF bypass capacitor near the supply pins to keep noise from a noisy or high-impedance supply out of the amplifier: a low-ESR ceramic from each supply pin to ground, as close to the package as possible. On a single supply, a lone capacitor between VCC+ and ground suffices.

Keep analog and digital grounds apart and mind the path of ground current; a ground plane on another layer spreads heat and lowers EMI pickup. Route inputs away from supply and output traces, crossing noisy traces at right angles where they must meet. Keep RF and RG next to the inverting input and keep input traces short, since inputs are the most sensitive nodes. Surrounding critical traces with a guard ring, driven at low impedance, reduces leakage from neighbouring traces at other potentials.

Pick supplies wider than both the input and output signal ranges; ±12 V suits a stage scaling ±0.5 V to ±1.8 V. Feedback resistors in the kilohm range suit the milliamp-level currents the stage carries.
Only the TL071C in the PS (SO-8) package brings out OFFSET N1 and OFFSET N2; a 100 kΩ potentiometer between them with its wiper to VCC- through 1.5 kΩ nulls the offset.
